reason: While the text clearly portrays the Hebrews as a distinct people (עִברִים appears multiple times), it does not depict them as a nation with its own specific land. The passage shows Hebrews in Egypt under Egyptian authority, bearing burdens and oppressed (סִבְלֹתָם - their burdens), without sovereignty or territorial possession. Moses subsequently flees to the land of Midian for refuge, not to any Hebrew territory. The text emphasizes Hebrew identity as a subjugated people under Egyptian rule, not as a nation in control of its own land.
